summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recent pericarditis, was admitted for abdominal pain and poor appetite following his last discharge. A CT scan revealed findings consistent with diverticulitis, and he was treated with IV antibiotics initially, followed by oral Augmentin. His abdominal pain resolved, and he tolerated oral intake well. Due to his history of recurrent C. diff, prophylactic oral vancomycin was added. His transplant kidney function remained stable at baseline, though renal ultrasound showed new changes in arterial resistive indices, which were monitored without intervention. The small pericardial effusion from prior admission persisted but remained stable without tamponade. He was discharged home on a full course of oral antibiotics with instructions to complete both Augmentin and vancomycin, and to schedule a follow-up colonoscopy.
problems: Diverticulitis of large intestine without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
